artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{LP}$ denote the Laguerre–Pólya class, i.e., the set of entire functions that are locally uniform limits of polynomials with only real zeros. Equivalently, $f\in\mathcal{LP}$ iff $f(x)=Cx^m e^{-\alpha x^2+\beta x}\prod_k (1-x/x_k)e^{x/x_k}$ with $C,\beta,x_k\in\mathbb{R}$, $\alpha\geq 0$, $m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$, and $\sum 1/x_k^2<\infty$.

Given a meromorphic function $F:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}\cup\{\infty\}$ whose poles avoid the nonnegative integers, define the linear operator $T_F$ acting on formal power series by
$$T_F\Big(\sum_{k\geq 0} a_k \frac{x^k}{k!}\Big) \;=\; \sum_{k\geq 0} F(k)\, a_k \frac{x^k}{k!}.$$

(a) Characterize all such meromorphic functions $F$ with the property that, whenever $\sum_{k\geq 0} a_k\,x^k/k!$ is a transcendental entire function with only real zeros (i.e., lies in $\mathcal{LP}$), the transformed series $\sum_{k\geq 0} F(k)\,a_k\,x^k/k!$ is again a transcendental entire function with only real zeros.

(b) Characterize all such meromorphic functions $F$ with the weaker property that, whenever $\sum_{k\geq 0} a_k\,x^k/k!\in\mathcal{LP}$, the transformed entire function $\sum_{k\geq 0} F(k)\,a_k\,x^k/k!$ has all its zeros in the open left half-plane $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\mathrm{Re}\,z<0\}$.
artifact.status_search_result: A direct web search did not surface a published characterization of meromorphic multipliers $F$ acting diagonally on exponential generating functions that preserve the Laguerre–Pólya class (or send it into functions with zeros in the open left half-plane). The classical Pólya–Schur theorem characterizes such multipliers among ordinary functions of $k$ for polynomials, but the meromorphic, transcendental EGF version stated here appears to remain an open characterization problem.
